name: Yatharth Srivastav
title: Developer & designer
intro: I build satellite trackers, voice interfaces, and small experiments for the web.
bio: I’m a student developer and designer in India. I like taking something hard to picture, like an orbit or a spoken command, and giving it an interface you can actually play with.
offscreen: Away from the keyboard, you’ll find me playing badminton, lifting, gaming, or catching up on anime.
journey: Published the first version of this site on GitHub Pages.
Added write-ups for ClaimGuard and ORBITAL, with a closer look at the design and development.
Added an orbit quiz to OrbytMax and tuned gesture recognition in Ultron.
Rebuilt the portfolio around five projects and an interactive signal experiment.
Turned the portfolio into a toy shelf with a gravity experiment, a handheld puzzle and a working typewriter.

projects.name: OrbytMax
projects.short: A satellite map with a reason to look up.
projects.problem: A dot on a map tells you very little about the spacecraft above you. OrbytMax connects the object to its mission and the next approximate visible pass over your city.
projects.approach: Start with the map, pick a satellite, then explore a mission or try the orbit basics quiz. City search falls back to a local list when geocoding is unavailable.
projects.captureAlt: OrbytMax mission library rendered from its local build.

projects.name: Ultron
projects.short: A Windows assistant that listens and watches locally.
projects.problem: Opening an app or triggering a shortcut usually means reaching for a mouse. Ultron explores voice and hand gestures as shortcuts for everyday desktop tasks.
projects.approach: Vosk recognizes speech while MediaPipe and OpenCV read hand gestures. A configurable command map connects each input to an explicit action, with a dry-run mode for testing.
projects.captureAlt: Transcript of the Ultron command-line help screen.

projects.name: ClaimGuard
projects.short: A review desk for the claims in product copy.
projects.problem: A small brand can easily lose the connection between a regulatory update and the copy it affects. This prototype puts both in one review workflow.
projects.approach: A category-specific feed surfaces updates. Reviewers can inspect a flagged claim, read a suggested rewrite and decide what to change before publishing.
projects.captureAlt: ClaimGuard landing page from the project’s screenshots.

projects.name: ORBITAL
projects.short: A globe that turns orbital data into motion.
projects.problem: Satellite catalogs are hard to read as tables. ORBITAL makes the paths visible on a globe so you can follow a single satellite in context.
projects.approach: Filter for Starlink, the ISS, GPS or weather satellites, then select an object to follow its path through the Three.js scene.
projects.captureAlt: ORBITAL project cover from the original portfolio.

projects.name: After You
projects.short: A typewriter for the words you’d leave behind.
projects.problem: What would you write for the next person at a typewriter? This small web experiment turns a short note into a paper snapshot.
projects.approach: Type a note and print a snapshot onto the page. Notes stay in your current session. The carriage control changes the position of the print head.
projects.captureAlt: A note printed in the After You browser experiment.
